__comment: Combined per manager request: Archiver, Archiver v2, and Enricher are three distinct backend worker services (different metric prefixes: archiver_*, connector_ingestion_times_seconds_* + kube_* for v2, enricher_ingestion_times_seconds_* for enricher) - not duplicates, so panels were not deduplicated, just laid out under one $datasource client picker. A single dropdown that swaps between the three panel sets isn't supported by this Grafana version's dashboard JSON schema without a plugin (it only works when all options share one query shape with a variable inside it, which isn't the case here since each service uses entirely different metric names) - so each service is its own section instead, click a row title to collapse/expand it. Archiver's own 5 sub-rows and Archiver v2's own 2 sub-rows are preserved as-is (Grafana does not support nesting a 'row' panel inside another collapsed row's panel list, so they're laid out as siblings under a plain section-title divider rather than force-wrapped in an outer collapsed row). $namespace/$pod were renamed per-service (archiver_namespace/archiver_pod, archiverv2_namespace/archiverv2_pod) to avoid the three dashboards' variables colliding now that they share one JSON file. PRE-EXISTING BUG FIXED: apps-archiver.json's 59 panels were actually two overlapping drafts of the same dashboard concatenated without adjusting coordinates (e.g. its 'Overview' row's CPU Usage stat at x=6,y=1 sat directly on top of the 'Health Status' row's Pods Running stat at the same x=6,y=1 - visually broken in Grafana). Kept only the richer draft (Health Status / Resource Consumption / Pulsar Messaging / What's Not Working / Custom Application Metrics - 38 panels); dropped the other draft's 21 panels (Overview / gRPC Metrics / Pulsar Integration / Resource Usage / Application Metrics / Database Connections / Logs & Errors) as stale/superseded. NOTE: apps-archiver.json and apps-archiverv2.json both defined their namespace/pod variables against job="archiver" (identical job name for both v1 and v2) - preserved as-is since the real job label wasn't ours to guess, but worth a second look.
